sources.excerpt: Octopuses have three hearts, and their blood is blue. A vibrant octopus with reddish-brown skin

reasoning: Octopuses indeed possess three hearts and blue blood. Two of these hearts (the branchial hearts) pump blood to the gills to absorb oxygen, while the third heart (the systemic heart) circulates the oxygenated blood to the rest of the body. Their blood is blue because it contains a copper-based protein called hemocyanin to transport oxygen, which turns blue when bound to oxygen and becomes colorless when deoxygenated (unlike the iron-based hemoglobin that makes human blood red). This is a well-established and universally accepted fact in marine biology.
